title_ar: الشيخ الددو ضيف دائم على قناة فور شباب طيلة أيام شهر رمضان في برنامج مفاهيم ج 4
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew a Standing Guest on the 4Shabab Channel throughout Ramadan, in the Programme Mafāhīm, Part 4
body_ar: تستضيف قناة فور شباب فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء في برنامج مفاهيم ( الجزء الرابع)، بوصفه ضيفا دائما للبرنامج، وذلك طيلة أيام شهر رمضان الكريم لهذا العام 1433 هـ، ويُحاور الشيخ في هذه الحلقات الدكتور عادل باناعمه. يبث هذا البرنامج كل يوم من أيام الشهر المبارك في الساعة الخامسة مساء بتوقيت مكة المكرمة، الثانية زوالا بالتوقيت العالمي، ويعاد بثه السادسة مساء بتوقيت مكة المكرمة، الثالثة صباحا بالتوقيت العالمي. ويهتم برنامج مفاهيم (الجزء الرابع)، بالمصطلحات والمفاهيم المتداولة في الوسط الشبابي بشكل عام، سواء كانت مفاهيم شرعية أو تربوية أو دعوية أو اجتماعية. حيث يسلط الضوء عليها من خلال تجلية معناها الصحيح وحدود تطبيقاتها المقبولة، والإشارة إلى ما يحصل فيها من خطأ على المستوى المعرفي أو المستوى التطبيقي، وذلك انطلاقا من الموازين الشرعية ومراعاة فقه الفتوى والواقع في المنهج الوسطي المعتدل. وقد تناولت الأجزاء الثلاثة السابقة من برنامج مفاهيم مواضيع مهمة، نذكر منها على سبيل المثال لا الحصر: - اتباع السلف. - الاختلاف الفقهي. - التدين والالتزام. - الجهاد. - الحرية. - العلاقة بين الرجل والمرأة. - الولاء والبراء. - الحسبة. - الذكر والدعاء. - زينة النساء. - قيام الليل. - حقوق المرأة. - الرياضة. - الديمقراطية. - الفن... ونشير كذلك إلى أن هناك برامج أخرى تبث في القنوات الأخرى للشيخ خلال الشهر الكريم منها قناة دليل وقناة الرسالة، وسيعلن عن مواعيدها في وقت لاحق قبل بثها، لذلك ننوه بأهميتها وندعو الجمهور الكريم إلى اغتنام هذه الفرصة الرمضانية الثمينة. وسيعمل القائمون على الموقع – إن شاء الله- على مواكبة حلقات هذا البرنامج وبثها مباشرة على الموقع ورفعها في القسم الخاص بها في جديد الموقع مع تلخيص لأهم أفكارها وتبسيط معانيها ليحصل النفع وتعم الفائدة.
body_en:
The 4Shabab channel is hosting Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, in the programme Mafāhīm (Part Four), as the programme's standing guest, throughout the days of the noble month of Ramadan of this year, 1433 AH. In these episodes the Sheikh is in conversation with Dr Adil Banaamah.

This programme is broadcast every day of the blessed month at five in the evening, Mecca time — two in the afternoon, universal time — and is rebroadcast at six in the evening, Mecca time — three in the morning, universal time.

Mafāhīm (Part Four) concerns itself with the terms and concepts in circulation in the youth milieu generally, whether those concepts belong to the Sharia, to upbringing, to the call to Islam (daʿwah) or to social life. It sheds light upon them by bringing out their correct meaning and the limits of their acceptable applications, and by pointing to the error that occurs in them at the level of knowledge or at the level of application — all of this proceeding from the criteria of the Sharia and with regard for the jurisprudence of issuing legal opinions and of the actual situation, within the moderate middle way.

The three preceding parts of Mafāhīm took up important subjects, of which we mention, by way of example and not exhaustively: following the forebears (salaf); jurisprudential difference; religiosity and commitment; jihad; freedom; the relationship between man and woman; loyalty and disavowal (al-walāʾ wa-l-barāʾ); the accountability of public conduct (ḥisbah); remembrance and supplication; women's adornment; the night prayer; women's rights; sport; democracy; art...

We note also that there are other programmes of the Sheikh's broadcast on other channels during the noble month, among them the Daleel channel and the al-Risalah channel; their times will be announced later, before they are broadcast. We therefore draw attention to their importance and invite the esteemed public to seize this precious Ramadan opportunity.

Those who run the site will, God willing, keep pace with this programme's episodes, broadcast them live on the site, and upload them to their own section among the site's new material, with a summary of their most important ideas and a simplification of their meanings, so that benefit may be obtained and advantage become general.

flags.arabic: - الجهاد. - الحرية. - الولاء والبراء. - الحسبة. - زينة النساء. - حقوق المرأة. - الديمقراطية. - الفن
flags.context: the list of subjects covered in the programme's earlier parts
options: render the list as served, as a list of titles with no content
treat the titles as indicating positions
flags.note: This is a list of fifteen subject headings and nothing more: jihad, loyalty and disavowal, women's adornment, women's rights, democracy and art among them. Every one of these is a subject on which the Sheikh's position would be quoted, and the corpus holds none of it — only that the programme discussed them. An English page carrying this list under his name invites readers to assume they will find his views behind it. Display must make clear that these are episode subjects, not positions, and should not link the headings to anything the corpus cannot supply.

options: the office of the market inspector
flags.note: ḥisbah is the institution of commanding right and forbidding wrong as a public office, historically that of the muḥtasib who supervised markets and public conduct. Style guide section 13 lists iḥtisāb, from the same root, as a pending glossary addition; ḥisbah itself is not in the glossary either. 'The enforcement of public morals' imports a coercive sense the term does not always carry; 'the accountability of public conduct' is used as the more neutral. Should be settled when iḥtisāb is added.

flags.context: the method the programme states for itself
options: with regard for the jurisprudence of issuing legal opinions and of the actual situation
taking into account the fiqh of fatwa and of reality
observing the jurisprudence of the fatwa and of the real world
flags.note: fiqh al-wāqiʿ, the jurisprudence of the actual situation, is a recognised pairing: the competence to read circumstances correctly before applying a ruling to them, as distinct from knowledge of the rulings themselves. The glossary carries fatwā as 'a considered legal opinion' and that is followed here. Neither fiqh al-wāqiʿ nor wasaṭiyyah (see record 796) is in the glossary, and this record uses both in one sentence; both should be added.

flags.arabic: السادسة مساء بتوقيت مكة المكرمة، الثالثة صباحا بالتوقيت العالمي
options: render the times as served and record the error
correct to three in the afternoon
flags.note: SOURCE ERROR, not corrected. Mecca is three hours ahead of universal time, and the same sentence gets the first pairing right: five in the evening in Mecca is two in the afternoon universal. Six in the evening in Mecca is therefore three in the afternoon, not three in the morning. The English carries the error as served, per style guide section 11.

flags.context: the first subject in the list
flags.note: The salaf are the earliest generations of Muslims. The phrase here names the practice of following them, not the modern movement that takes its name from them, and 'Salafism' would import a contemporary alignment the Arabic does not state. 'Forebears' rather than 'predecessors' is used for plainness. Not in the glossary.

translator_notes: A site announcement of a Ramadan broadcast schedule. It carries no religious content of the Sheikh's, but it lists fifteen subjects he has treated on air, and is the corpus's best index of what the Mafāhīm programme covered.
The CMS timestamp, 21 July 2012, is a bulk-upload date; Ramadan 1433 began on or about 20 July 2012.
'مفاهيم' means 'Concepts'; the programme is known by its Arabic name and the name is kept, transliterated, rather than translated. See also record 787, a tribute occasioned by this same programme.

The final paragraph is the site's undertaking to publish summaries of every episode. Whether it was kept is worth checking: this slice contains no such summaries, and the corpus inventory's count of title-only stubs may include them.
